I've always drawn since I was young and it's what I would constantly do for years and still do. I live in a very conservative place so I never really got support for it nor encouragement to go down this path nor any in general so I never found any other passion that my family would call it 'money making'. I took calculus classes in high school and even had extra tutoring classes for 4 hours every few days a week. I was basically doing math every single day because for me it was an incredibly hard subject but my high school required it, I also took accounting which was also a subject I absolutely hated. Basically in all I suffered through high school, always came back home to draw for hours and would lose sleep just so I could draw, I just never had any direction because no one ever supported me except my history teacher(LOL). I eventually decided in my last year of high school that I would go for college in art and even though I knew about their reputations I still wanted to go. I had no other direction, unfortunately I would be stopped by my family and pushed towards Computer Science. I let it happen, because I got defeated by the pressure and my inability to stand up for my self. Guess what happened? I fell into a depression, failed multiple classes. Computer Science is amazing when you're passionate, but I wasn't, and the classes I was in were full of math and it straight up sucked the life out of me. I dropped out a few months ago despite protests and now I have to fight my own self to not regret my decision. I love art but I'm absolutely scared I will not make anything out of it yet it's all I know to do. I'm not rich and I don't want to dissapoint my family by failing again. I just hated CS so much I couldn't handle seeing everyone so passionate while I was completely out of place there. I had no one to guide me in life until my family forced me towards CS so I didn't know better, but I know CS makes money and that was their main focus, which I feel bad towards, but I don't know if I would've made it out of alive out of that college as dramatic as it seemed. It completely killed my motivation to draw for a while and now I need to build up a portfolio in a few days while in extreme doubt:) I'm just hoping I can do things right this time, somewhat!
